findings.issue_text: [BUG] import_remote calls open(url).read but topic_embed.rb only require_dependency's nokogiri and never require's 'open-uri', so Kernel#open falls back to plain file semantics. In a fresh process (e.g. the disqus thor task, which does `require './config/environment'` and nothing else that guarantees open-uri, or a Rails console), open('http://eviltrout.com/123') treats the URL as a filename and raises Errno::ENOENT instead of fetching the article, so embed retrieval crashes.

[BUG] The migration defaults posts.cook_method to 1, but Post.cook_methods assigns :regular=0 and :raw_html=1, so the migration labels every pre-existing post as raw_html. After migrating, every existing post's cook() returns raw markdown instead of cooked HTML (Post#cook short-circuits on cook_method == raw_html), silently breaking rendering of the entire post corpus; the default should be 0 (:regular).

[ADVISORY] poll_feed assumes every feed item exposes i.content, but SimpleRSS items raise NoMethodError for tags the feed does not define (many RSS 2.0 feeds only have description, Atom uses summary/content variants). The first item lacking a content element raises NoMethodError, aborting the whole poll cycle (sidekiq retry: false, so the batch is silently skipped and no items after the failure import); author's strongest rebuttal — that target feeds always have content — fails because the setting invites arbitrary feed URLs.

[ADVISORY] ruby-readability and simple-rss are added to the Gemfile but only Gemfile_rails4.lock is updated; the primary Gemfile.lock is left stale. Bundler on the non-rails4 lock path reports the lockfile as out of sync with the Gemfile and aborts `bundle install` / `bundle exec` until someone regenerates Gemfile.lock, breaking CI and fresh checkouts on that path.

[BUG] PollFeed calls CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) on feed items whose entry has no content element (standard RSS 2.0 uses description, not content), raising NoMethodError on nil and aborting the whole poll run. Any feed where an item lacks <content> makes SimpleRSS return nil for i.content; the job raises NoMethodError, and since sidekiq_options retry: false is set, the run silently dies before processing remaining items, so no topics are imported until the feed changes.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import stores third-party feed/HTML content as a post with cook_method :raw_html and Post#cook returns raw unfiltered, with no sanitize step anywhere in the import path. Arbitrary HTML/JavaScript from a remote RSS feed or imported article is stored as the post body and rendered via `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb (and everywhere cooked posts render), letting the feed publisher inject script into pages served on the forum's origin — a stored XSS vector gated only by the admin choosing to enable feed polling.

[BUG] The embed layout interpolates request.referer raw into a JavaScript string literal (<%= request.referer %>), and ERb HTML-escaping does not escape single quotes, so a crafted Referer header breaks out of the string. An attacker who controls the Referer header sent to /embed/best (the header is fully attacker-supplied in real browsers/curl) can inject arbitrary JavaScript into the embed page served on the forum's origin, despite ensure_embeddable only comparing the host — any URL whose host matches embeddable_host with a malicious path/query fragment gets through.

[BUG] The loading view reloads every 30 seconds unconditionally with no terminal failure state, even when retrieval can never succeed. When fetch_http bails (embed_by_username unset or user not found), TopicRetriever's host check rejects the URL, the throttle blocks the retry, or import fails, the embedded iframe shows 'Loading Discussion...' and re-requests /embed/best (enqueuing a retrieve job each time) forever on the publisher's page — an infinite reload loop with no error surfaced to the embedding site.

[BUG] EmbedController#best builds TopicView.new(topic_id, ...) for whatever topic_id TopicEmbed returns with no guard that the topic still exists or is readable. If the embedded topic is deleted after the topic_embeds row is created (or the row's topic_id is otherwise dangling), TopicView.new raises (RecordNotFound/ArgumentError) and the embed endpoint returns a 500 rendered inside the publisher's iframe; likewise post.user.small_avatar_url at line 20 raises NoMethodError when a post's author has been deleted, killing the whole embed render.

[ADVISORY] The new RetrieveTopic job has no spec anywhere in this diff (spec/jobs contains only poll_feed_spec.rb), leaving its user_id lookup and no_throttle/staff branching untested. A regression in the user_id→User lookup or the no_throttle: user.try(:staff?) logic (e.g. throttling bypass silently applying to all users or none) ships undetected, and every future change to this job is made with no safety net.

[ADVISORY] TopicEmbed.import_remote (the path used by both TopicRetriever.fetch_http and the Disqus importer) has no test coverage in this diff. The readability extraction pipeline — tag whitelist, title fallback, open() fetch — is exercised by no spec, so a regression in content extraction or the fetch silently corrupts imported posts; note also that import_remote calls open(url) without requiring 'open-uri' (only poll_feed.rb requires it), so the method depends on incidental load order to avoid NameError.

[ADVISORY] poll_feed has no error handling around open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) or SimpleRSS.parse, and the job sets retry: false. A transient feed outage (timeout, DNS failure, malformed XML) raises, the run is not retried, and the failure is invisible except in logs — an operator with feed_polling_enabled gets no signal that imports stopped, and topics silently diverge from the feed for up to an hour (or indefinitely if the feed stays broken).

[ADVISORY] The Disqus importer silently loses its --category option and its permalink-post behavior, switching creation to TopicEmbed.import_remote with no migration note for existing callers. Existing automation invoking `thor disqus:import -c "Some Category"` now fails with an unknown-option error, and previously imported Disqus threads (which got a Permalink link post) would now create raw-HTML embed topics instead — a behavioral change to a public CLI surface with no counterpart or deprecation path in this diff.

[ADVISORY] Feed items whose link resolves to blank and whose id is also non-HTTP produce url = i.id / nil, and items with a blank or missing title flow into PostCreator under skip_validations: true. With validations skipped, a nil/blank title is not rejected by PostCreator's normal validation, so malformed feed entries can create topics with empty titles (or fail inside the transaction each hour, re-enqueueing the same bad item every poll with no dead-letter or skip counter), poisoning the import stream indefinitely.

[BUG] The migration sets posts.cook_method default to 1, but Post.cook_methods Enum maps :regular to 0 and :raw_html to 1, so every existing and new post defaults to cook_method == raw_html. app/models/post.rb cook() returns raw for cook_method == :raw_html, so every normal post created after this migration skips the entire cooking/markdown/sanitization pipeline and is rendered as-is — all user-authored markdown breaks and unsanitized HTML is rendered site-wide.

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import stores third-party RSS/article HTML as the post's raw content with cook_method raw_html and skip_validations: true, bypassing Discourse's sanitizer, and app/views/embed/best.html.erb renders it with raw post.cooked. Any hostile or compromised feed/embedded source can inject arbitrary script into the post content; it renders inside the embed iframe (and the topic page), giving stored XSS on the Discourse origin.

[BUG] The diff removes the --category option, its category_id lookup, and the PostCreator permalink format from the Disqus importer, rewriting it to TopicEmbed.import_remote — work not traceable to the stated 'enhance embed URL handling and validation' intent. Users' existing disqus:import invocations with -c now fail with an unknown-option error, and imported topics silently lose their Permalink preamble and category placement; this is an unrelated breaking change hidden in an embedding PR.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds force: true to create_table :top_topics, an unrelated change that drops and recreates the table on every migrate. Any operator re-running migrations (or a fresh migrate on an environment where the table already exists with data) silently destroys all existing top_topics aggregates; nothing in the embedding feature requires this table change.

[ADVISORY] The only changes to the MigrateWordCounts migration are whitespace and removal of the trailing newline — unrelated churn in a data migration. Reviewers and git blame for a migration that already ran in production get polluted with a no-op edit; if anyone re-runs or cherry-picks this migration, the diff gives no signal of what changed (nothing should have).

[ADVISORY] New runtime dependencies ruby-readability and simple-rss are added but only Gemfile_rails4.lock is updated; the primary Gemfile.lock is not in the diff. Non-Rails4 installs cannot resolve the new gems from their stale lockfile, breaking bundle install on the main deployment path until the lock is regenerated.

[ADVISORY] PollFeed#import unconditionally calls i.content.scrub, but feed items without a content element will raise NoMethodError on nil, aborting the whole hourly poll. A single feed item lacking <content> (link/title-only feeds are common) makes every subsequent poll crash at i.content, so no further feed items are ever imported until the feed changes; also i.id fallback for non-http links is untested.

[ADVISORY] EmbedController#best enqueues a retrieve job and renders 'loading' for any embed_url on the embeddable host, with no validation that the URL is well-formed or reachable before enqueueing. Arbitrary garbage URLs matching the host are pushed into sidekiq where TopicRetriever must reject them; the referrer-only host check means any page on the embeddable host can enqueue unlimited retrieval jobs (the 60s throttle only applies per-URL to non-staff users), letting a page spam the job queue and outbound fetches.

[BUG] poll_feed calls CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) without guarding against feeds whose items have no content element, so a nil content raises NoMethodError and aborts the entire hourly import mid-loop. Any feed entry lacking <content> (link-only feeds are common) crashes the job before later items are processed; with sidekiq_options retry: false the feed silently stops importing every hour until the feed changes or someone debugs the logs — and each crash point advances as earlier items got imported, producing partial, order-dependent state.

[BUG] On the update path, TopicEmbed.import writes content_sha1 via embed.update_column unconditionally after revisor.revise!, without checking whether the revision succeeded, so the stored sha1 can come to match content that was never actually persisted to the post. If revise! fails (validation, exception in the cooking pipeline, etc.), content_sha1 now equals the digest of the new remote contents while the post still holds the old raw text; the next poll computes the same sha1, skips the revision, and the source article's change is permanently lost — external edits are silently swallowed with no error anywhere.

[BUG] The resize postMessage uses the full referer URL ('<%= request.referer %>') as targetOrigin instead of the parent page's origin, which never matches the receiving document's origin when the referer contains a path. For any embedding page deeper than the site root, the browser drops the 'discourse-resize' message because the targetOrigin (scheme+host+path) does not equal the parent window's origin, so iframe.height is never set and the embedded comments render at the default/clipped height for the majority of embeds.

[BUG] The postMessage origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring containment test, not an origin equality test, so any origin that appears anywhere inside discourseUrl passes. A hostile embedding page whose origin is a substring of discourseUrl (trivially, any page when discourseUrl is short or when e.origin is a prefix like 'https://for') can post forged {type:'discourse-resize'} messages that control the iframe's rendered height — the boundary check the code exists to enforce does not actually bind the message to the Discourse origin.

[ADVISORY] feed_key builds a per-feed Redis key ('feed-modified:<sha1>') that nothing in the diff ever reads or writes — it is phantom infrastructure for conditional polling that was never wired up. The next contributor assumes last-modified tracking exists (the method's name and SHA1-of-URL key imply it) and builds on it, or wastes time figuring out why the feed is fully re-parsed every hour; delete the method or use it.

[ADVISORY] import is check-then-create on embed_url (WHERE first, then create!) with no rescue of the unique-index violation, so two concurrent imports of the same URL collide on the unique index. EmbedController enqueues a RetrieveTopic job per viewer for a not-yet-imported article; two viewers within the throttle window (the 60s Redis setnx throttle is per-process-order, and the PollFeed path runs concurrently with fetch_http) both pass the exists? check and one TopicEmbed.create! raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, killing the job after PostCreator has already committed a topic — leaving an orphan topic and a viewer whose loading page reloads forever.

[ADVISORY] ensure_embeddable compares URI(request.referer).host by exact string equality with SiteSetting.embeddable_host, with no normalization for case, port, or www prefix, and the setting has no place to express scheme or port. An embedding site served from www.eviltrout.com, from a non-default port, or with an uppercase host configured fails the referer check and 404s its embeds; conversely the same loose equality is the only access control for the endpoint, so the drift between how operators type the setting and how browsers emit referers decides who can embed — a configuration minefield rather than a real invariant.

[ADVISORY] poll_feed iterates the entire feed with no item cap or last-modified cutoff, and TopicEmbed.import does a fresh SELECT + SHA1 per item every hour regardless of change. A large feed causes an hourly O(N) full pass with one query per item and one PostRevisor pass per changed item on whatever single process runs the scheduled job; nothing in the design bounds the work, so feed size directly scales background cost with no pagination or batching escape hatch.

[ADVISORY] The loading page reloads every 30 seconds forever with no terminal state or error signal when retrieval never produces a topic. When fetch_http bails silently (embed_by_username blank, readability returns nothing, the remote URL 404s), TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed stays nil on every reload and the embedding page shows 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely, with the client polling the server forever — the async chain has no failure representation at the consumer boundary.

[ADVISORY] Deduplication is keyed on the raw embed_url string with exact equality, so the same article reached via variant spellings (trailing slash, case differences in path, i.link vs i.id forms from PollFeed's fallback) imports as separate topics. PollFeed normalizes nothing before calling import (it even substitutes i.id for i.link), so the same article can be imported twice as two duplicate topics, and the unique index on embed_url that exists to prevent duplicates only prevents exact-string duplicates — the domain identity of 'this article' is not representable in the key.

[ADVISORY] The disqus import task silently drops its --category option and switches its code path to TopicEmbed.import_remote, changing the created posts' cook_method and permalink shape for existing task users. Anyone with a scripted `disqus import -c Category` invocation gets an unrecognized-option failure (or silent ignoring depending on Thor version), and posts created after the change are raw_html imports with an 'Imported from' footer rather than plain cooked posts — an unversioned behavioral break of a maintained entry point.

[ADVISORY] The `--category`/`-c` CLI option and its handling code were deleted from the disqus import task, silently removing a previously working public interface without any replacement or migration note. Existing users/scripts that invoke `thor disqus:import -c Category` break with an unknown-option error on upgrade; the review iteration changed the task's contract with no explicit acceptance of that removal.

[ADVISORY] The import loop's behavior was silently rewritten from creating a lightweight permalink post (`PostCreator.new(user, title:..., raw: "\[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})\]")`) to calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which performs a blocking HTTP fetch per thread and imports full article HTML. Operators who re-run a previously working Disqus import get a different artifact than before: network-dependent imports (can hang/fail per URL), raw-HTML posts bypassing the cooking pipeline, and topics created via the embed path — a changed output contract never surfaced as a decision point.

[ADVISORY] An already-shipped migration was edited to add `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics`, changing its semantics from create-if-absent to drop-and-recreate. Any environment that has not yet run this migration loses existing `top_topics` data when it runs; this edit rode along inside an unrelated embedding PR with no stated intent to alter the migration's behavior.

[ADVISORY] An already-shipped migration file was touched in this PR purely for whitespace and removal of the trailing newline, a no-op edit unrelated to the embedding feature. The diff carries silent noise that misrepresents what the PR does: future git blame/bisect on this migration points at the embedding change, and reviewers waste effort hunting for a behavioral change that does not exist.

[BUG] cook_method == raw_html returns the post raw, bypassing the entire sanitize/render pipeline, and TopicEmbed.import sets this for all externally-fetched RSS/article content, which is then emitted with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in embed views. Any attacker-controlled markup in the polled feed or in a page fetched by TopicRetriever (script tags, event handlers, javascript: hrefs) is stored and rendered unsanitized on /embed/best — a persistent XSS executing in the embeddable_host origin, the origin that third-party sites iframe by design. skip_validations: true on both create and revise removes the last guard.

[BUG] import interpolates the raw embed URL into an HTML attribute without escaping: `"#{url}"`, and the only gate is the regex `/^https?\:\/\//` which permits quotes, spaces, and angle brackets in the URL. A feed item link like `http://x/'onmouseover='alert(document.cookie)//` passes the scheme regex, is stored via the raw_html cook path without sanitization, and produces an injected attribute/element in the rendered post — stored XSS on the embed page triggered by any feed-supplied link.

[BUG] import_remote calls `open(url).read` with no redirect, IP, or scheme constraint; the host allowlist is checked earlier in TopicRetriever against the original URL only, but open() silently follows redirects and re-resolves DNS. A page on embeddable_host (or any attacker page whose referer matches embeddable_host) can trigger a server-side fetch that 302-redirects (or DNS-rebinds after the host check) to 169.254.169.254, localhost, or internal services; the response body is parsed by Readability and portions (title/content) end up rendered in the embed page, leaking internal network data via SSRF. Note the /^https?\/\// gate in import runs only after the fetch has already happened.

[ADVISORY] `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` fetches an admin-set config URL with no scheme validation and no SSRF guard, and its content is fed to SimpleRSS and then into raw_html posts. SiteSetting.feed_polling_url is config-backed attacker-controllable input in the threat model: a compromised admin session (or XSS in the admin UI) can point it at an internal endpoint to exfiltrate response data through imported topics, or at a feed whose items carry XSS payloads that the raw_html path renders verbatim (see the cook_method bypass).

[ADVISORY] postMessage origin validation uses `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, a substring containment test instead of an equality test against a parsed origin. The check accepts any e.origin that appears anywhere inside the discourseUrl string rather than matching the exact origin, so any embedding page whose origin is a substring of the configured URL (e.g. a subdomain sibling sharing the suffix) can post fabricated resize messages. Impact is limited to iframe height spoofing, but the containment comparison is the wrong control shape.

[ADVISORY] The embed authorization control compares `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` without normalizing case or trailing port, while the same host string is checked again in TopicRetriever#invalid_host? — two independently hand-maintained copies of the host allowlist. An admin who stores embeddable_host with different case or an explicit port from what browsers send in Referer gets a silent total lockout of embedding (availability failure of the control rather than a bypass), and any future tightening of one check (e.g. scheme validation) silently diverges from the other, which is exactly the drift that later produces a bypass.

[ADVISORY] The two 'valid host' tests stub the private methods under test (retrieved_recently? and perform_retrieve), so the assertions are tautologies that verify nothing about the real code. 'calls perform_retrieve if it hasn't been retrieved recently' stubs retrieved_recently? to return false and then asserts perform_retrieve is called — the test passes even if the real retrieve logic is inverted or broken, because the real gate and the real redis setnx/expire throttle logic are never executed. The actual throttle semantics (60s window, no_throttle override for staff, redis key leak on setnx without expire) have zero coverage in this diff.

[ADVISORY] Every test in poll_feed_spec stubs poll_feed out, so the entire body of the new poll_feed method (RSS parsing, url fallback to i.id, content scrubbing, TopicEmbed.import invocation) is never executed by any test. The 'delegates to poll_feed' test only proves execute calls a method — the real RSS-handling logic added in this diff (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:27-39), including the i.link/i.id fallback and CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) which crashes on feeds whose items lack a content element, ships with no test that would catch a regression.

[ADVISORY] The 'creates a topic view when a topic_id is found' test verifies only that the TopicView.new mock was constructed with specific args, asserting the mock interaction rather than any rendered behavior. The real TopicView is never built and the embed/best.html.erb template (new in this diff) is never rendered with real data — the view's posts.present? branching, avatar/username rendering, and the case where a topic exists with zero posts (the 'start_discussion' branch) are all untested and would break silently.

[ADVISORY] The error-path assertions use bare response.should_not be_success, which passes for any non-2xx outcome and does not verify the specific 404/InvalidAccess contract the tests claim to check. The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test would still pass if params.require(:embed_url) produced an unhandled 500 instead of the intended 404 — the tests cannot distinguish the promised error semantics from a crash, giving false confidence in the ensure_embeddable error path.

[ADVISORY] The update test asserts the revised content but never asserts that content_sha1 was persisted or that importing identical content skips the revision, leaving the new sha1-comparison branch half-verified. A regression in the content_sha1 update (topic_embed.rb:44 embed.update_column) or in the unchanged-content short-circuit (content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1) would pass this suite — e.g. if update_column were removed, every poll would silently rewrite the post and the tests would still be green; the 'import is idempotent' property the sha1 exists to provide is never asserted.

[BUG] add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1 sets every existing post to cook_method=1, which per Post.cook_methods Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) is :raw_html. After this migration runs, every pre-existing post in the database is silently reclassified as raw HTML: Post#cook (app/models/post.rb:131-134) returns raw uncooked text for cook_method == :raw_html, so all historical markdown posts render their raw markdown source to users. The default should be 0 (:regular); the migration backfills the entire table with the wrong value and there is no correcting backfill step.

[BUG] An already-shipped migration is modified in this diff to add force: true to create_table :top_topics. Any environment that re-runs this migration (e.g. migrating a database where the version row was rolled back, or a deploy replay) executes DROP TABLE top_topics and recreates it, destroying all computed top-topic ranking data with no backup or export step. A shipped migration must never be made destructive; the force: true flag belongs only in the new migration for fresh environments, not by editing the historical one.

[ADVISORY] create_table :topic_embeds uses force: true, making the migration destructive on re-run, and the table defines topic_id/post_id as plain integers with no foreign keys or dependent cleanup. Re-running the migration drops any populated topic_embeds rows (losing the embed_url→topic mapping, which then causes TopicRetriever/EmbedController to re-import duplicate topics). Additionally, when a topic or post is deleted there is no cascade or cleanup hook, leaving orphaned topic_embeds rows whose topic_id_for_embed lookups return dead topic ids for EmbedController#best.

[BUG] The throttle key is committed via $redis.setnx before perform_retrieve runs, so a failed or failed-early retrieval still marks the embed_url as 'retrieved' and blocks all retries for 60 seconds If import_remote raises or the user lookup returns nil on the first attempt, subsequent embed page loads within 60s skip retrieval entirely; the throttle key expires but each retry re-arms it, so a persistently failing URL is retried at most once per 60s per visitor with no error recorded anywhere

[BUG] The update path advances embed.content_sha1 to the new digest even when revisor.revise! returns false without revising (should_revise? false, e.g. post deleted), permanently discarding the new content Once the sha1 is updated while the post write was skipped, every future poll sees an unchanged digest and the remote article's edits are silently dropped forever while the feed poll reports success

[BUG] poll_feed has no error handling around the parse or per-item import loop and the job is declared sidekiq_options retry: false, so any single malformed item (nil content -> NoMethodError on i.content.scrub, or a non-HTTP i.id GUID like 'tag:...') aborts the remaining items with no retry and no user-visible error One bad feed entry silently drops the rest of that poll cycle every hour; items after the failing one are never imported and nothing surfaces the failure to the operator

[BUG] import_remote calls open(url).read with no timeout and no size cap on a user-triggered path (the embed controller enqueues RetrieveTopic for every visitor URL) A slow or hanging remote host blocks the Sidekiq worker indefinitely (open-uri default has no read timeout for this usage), and a huge response is fully read into memory before parsing, exhausting the worker

[BUG] open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) has no timeout or download-size cap on the hourly scheduled job A hung or enormous feed permanently wedges the PollFeed scheduled worker slot each cycle instead of failing fast

[BUG] The loading page reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely and the retrieval job's failure (invalid host, nil user, fetch error, throttled skip) never renders any error or terminal state When retrieval fails permanently the embedding site shows an endless 'Loading Discussion...' loop with no indication anything is wrong, and every reload re-enqueues a RetrieveTopic job forever

[BUG] When PostCreator#create returns nil inside the transaction, the code silently continues (embed never created, post stays nil) and import returns nil with no log or error result PollFeed treats the item as processed and moves on; the embed page keeps serving the loading loop with no record that topic creation failed

[BUG] The update path calls embed.post and passes it to PostRevisor without a nil check, so a deleted post raises NoMethodError inside the poll/retrieve job A remote article whose topic was deleted makes every PollFeed cycle and every RetrieveTopic job for that URL raise, repeatedly failing the job with a raw exception instead of a handled skip

[ADVISORY] feed_key is dead code: it is defined but never called anywhere in the diff, and the Modified-since behavior it implies (skipping unchanged feeds) was never implemented The next maintainer assumes feed polling is incremental because the key exists and builds on it; deleting the method removes the misleading implication at zero cost

[ADVISORY] The fallback 'url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?/' assigns the entry id, which for Atom feeds is commonly a non-URL URN (tag:...), and TopicEmbed.import then silently returns nil for it with no log Atom feeds whose ids are URNs are silently skipped every hour with no error result and no log line identifying which item was dropped

[ADVISORY] Every visitor to a not-yet-imported embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job (throttled only by the 60s redis key for non-staff), and the throttle key persists even when retrieval fails, coupling page-render behavior to job success with no observability on the enqueue path A popularly-linked but unimportable URL generates a continuous stream of jobs and reloads that all end in the loading loop, with no counter or log distinguishing 'not yet imported' from 'permanently failing'

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] On the update path, TopicEmbed.import writes content_sha1 via embed.update_column unconditionally after revisor.revise!, without checking whether the revision succeeded, so the stored sha1 can come to match content that was never actually persisted to the post. If revise! fails (validation, exception in the cooking pipeline, etc.), content_sha1 now equals the digest of the new remote contents while the post still holds the old raw text; the next poll computes the same sha1, skips the revision, and the source article's change is permanently lost — external edits are silently swallowed with no error anywhere.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`’s update branch, when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`, it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then immediately does `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` without checking any return value or success condition from `revise!`/the underlying save (`PostRevisor#update_post` now uses `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, which can return `false`). If `revise!` returns `false` (e.g., `should_revise?` fails) or the save fails without raising, `content_sha1` will still be updated, allowing future polls to skip revisions even though the post content was not actually updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The resize postMessage uses the full referer URL ('<%= request.referer %>') as targetOrigin instead of the parent page's origin, which never matches the receiving document's origin when the referer contains a path. For any embedding page deeper than the site root, the browser drops the 'discourse-resize' message because the targetOrigin (scheme+host+path) does not equal the parent window's origin, so iframe.height is never set and the embedded comments render at the default/clipped height for the majority of embeds.
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes the same bug: using the full referrer URL as postMessage targetOrigin (including path) instead of the origin (scheme+host+port), causing the browser to drop the message and preventing iframe resizing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The postMessage origin check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring containment test, not an origin equality test, so any origin that appears anywhere inside discourseUrl passes. A hostile embedding page whose origin is a substring of discourseUrl (trivially, any page when discourseUrl is short or when e.origin is a prefix like 'https://for') can post forged {type:'discourse-resize'} messages that control the iframe's rendered height — the boundary check the code exists to enforce does not actually bind the message to the Discourse origin.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the message handler validates origin with `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }`, which is a substring containment check rather than an equality check against the expected Discourse origin. This means a different (attacker-controlled) origin that happens to be a substring of `discourseUrl` would be accepted and could send forged `{type: 'discourse-resize'}` messages to control `iframe.height`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key builds a per-feed Redis key ('feed-modified:<sha1>') that nothing in the diff ever reads or writes — it is phantom infrastructure for conditional polling that was never wired up. The next contributor assumes last-modified tracking exists (the method's name and SHA1-of-URL key imply it) and builds on it, or wastes time figuring out why the feed is fully re-parsed every hour; delete the method or use it.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb a `feed_key` method is introduced that constructs a Redis key (`"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)}"`), but nothing in this diff ever calls `feed_key` or reads/writes that Redis key. `poll_feed` always parses the feed via `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and iterates items with no conditional/last-modified logic. This is dead/unused infrastructure that could mislead future contributors, but it does not break current behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] import is check-then-create on embed_url (WHERE first, then create!) with no rescue of the unique-index violation, so two concurrent imports of the same URL collide on the unique index. EmbedController enqueues a RetrieveTopic job per viewer for a not-yet-imported article; two viewers within the throttle window (the 60s Redis setnx throttle is per-process-order, and the PollFeed path runs concurrently with fetch_http) both pass the exists? check and one TopicEmbed.create! raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, killing the job after PostCreator has already committed a topic — leaving an orphan topic and a viewer whose loading page reloads forever.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` and implements `TopicEmbed.import` as a check-then-create (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then `TopicEmbed.create!`). There is no rescue/handling for `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`, so concurrent imports of the same URL (e.g., a scheduled `Jobs::PollFeed` run and a `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`/`TopicRetriever` fetch happening at the same time) can raise on the unique constraint and fail the job/request path. Some details in the finding (e.g., Redis throttle being per-process, and guaranteed orphan topics) aren’t fully proven from this diff, but the unhandled uniqueness race itself is verifiable from the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ensure_embeddable compares URI(request.referer).host by exact string equality with SiteSetting.embeddable_host, with no normalization for case, port, or www prefix, and the setting has no place to express scheme or port. An embedding site served from www.eviltrout.com, from a non-default port, or with an uppercase host configured fails the referer check and 404s its embeds; conversely the same loose equality is the only access control for the endpoint, so the drift between how operators type the setting and how browsers emit referers decides who can embed — a configuration minefield rather than a real invariant.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, the referer allowlist check is a strict host string comparison: `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and `embeddable_host` is configured as a plain host string in `config/site_settings.yml`. This can indeed be brittle for common operator/config variants like `www.` vs apex domains (different host strings) and generally lacks any normalization/allowlist flexibility. However, parts of the finding overstate/incorrectly claim port/scheme issues: the code compares only `.host` (not port), so a non-default port in the referer would not fail this check. This is best framed as a configuration/edge-case robustness concern rather than a clearly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] poll_feed iterates the entire feed with no item cap or last-modified cutoff, and TopicEmbed.import does a fresh SELECT + SHA1 per item every hour regardless of change. A large feed causes an hourly O(N) full pass with one query per item and one PostRevisor pass per changed item on whatever single process runs the scheduled job; nothing in the design bounds the work, so feed size directly scales background cost with no pagination or batching escape hatch.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows Jobs::PollFeed is scheduled hourly and unconditionally does `rss.items.each` over the entire parsed feed (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`) with no cap, pagination, or last-modified/ETag cutoff (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). For each item it calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and computes `Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)` every time; if content changed it runs a `PostRevisor` update (app/models/topic_embed.rb). This makes the job cost scale linearly with feed size each hour and introduces one DB lookup per item, which is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/architecture concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The loading page reloads every 30 seconds forever with no terminal state or error signal when retrieval never produces a topic. When fetch_http bails silently (embed_by_username blank, readability returns nothing, the remote URL 404s), TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed stays nil on every reload and the embedding page shows 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely, with the client polling the server forever — the async chain has no failure representation at the consumer boundary.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an embed loading flow that can loop indefinitely with no terminal/error state: when `EmbedController#best` can’t find a topic (`TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` nil) it enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` and renders `embed/loading` (new). That loading view unconditionally reloads the page every 30s (`setTimeout(... document.location.reload(), 30000)`). On the backend, `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` can silently no-op when the configured user is missing (`return if user.blank?`), and `perform_retrieve` can exit without creating an embed if prerequisites aren’t met (e.g., no user). Nothing in the controller/view surfaces failure, so the client will keep polling forever if retrieval never results in a `TopicEmbed` row. This is a diff-grounded missing failure/timeout representation rather than a provable logic error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Deduplication is keyed on the raw embed_url string with exact equality, so the same article reached via variant spellings (trailing slash, case differences in path, i.link vs i.id forms from PollFeed's fallback) imports as separate topics. PollFeed normalizes nothing before calling import (it even substitutes i.id for i.link), so the same article can be imported twice as two duplicate topics, and the unique index on embed_url that exists to prevent duplicates only prevents exact-string duplicates — the domain identity of 'this article' is not representable in the key.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, deduplication is `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and the DB enforces uniqueness only on the exact `embed_url` string (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` passes through `i.link` but will substitute `i.id` when `link` is blank or not http(s), and does no URL canonicalization (no normalization of trailing slashes, case, etc.). Since `TopicEmbed.import` also does not normalize, the same underlying article reachable via variant URL spellings can be imported as separate topics, which is duplicate/broken behavior relative to the intent of the unique index.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The disqus import task silently drops its --category option and switches its code path to TopicEmbed.import_remote, changing the created posts' cook_method and permalink shape for existing task users. Anyone with a scripted `disqus import -c Category` invocation gets an unrecognized-option failure (or silent ignoring depending on Thor version), and posts created after the change are raw_html imports with an 'Imported from' footer rather than plain cooked posts — an unversioned behavioral break of a maintained entry point.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` line is removed and all logic that reads `options[:category]` and passes `category: category_id` into `PostCreator` is deleted. The import path is switched to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`, which ultimately creates posts via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and appends an "Imported from" footer in `TopicEmbed.import`. This is a concrete backward-incompatible change to the existing `disqus import` CLI entry point: `-c/--category` is no longer accepted and imported post content/cooking behavior changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `--category`/`-c` CLI option and its handling code were deleted from the disqus import task, silently removing a previously working public interface without any replacement or migration note. Existing users/scripts that invoke `thor disqus:import -c Category` break with an unknown-option error on upgrade; the review iteration changed the task's contract with no explicit acceptance of that removal.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Disqus Thor task CLI interface for `--category`/`-c`: `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` is deleted and the `options[:category]` handling / `category_id` lookup code is removed in `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`. With this change, existing invocations like `thor disqus:import -c Category` would now fail with an unknown-option error, which is a backwards-incompatible contract change rather than an internal correctness defect evidenced elsewhere in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The import loop's behavior was silently rewritten from creating a lightweight permalink post (`PostCreator.new(user, title:..., raw: "\[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})\]")`) to calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which performs a blocking HTTP fetch per thread and imports full article HTML. Operators who re-run a previously working Disqus import get a different artifact than before: network-dependent imports (can hang/fail per URL), raw-HTML posts bypassing the cooking pipeline, and topics created via the embed path — a changed output contract never surfaced as a decision point.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` changed from creating a simple permalink post via `PostCreator.new(... raw: "\[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})\]")` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (blocking network fetch) and then imports `doc.content` through `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, and `Post#cook` now returns `raw` for `raw_html` (bypassing the cooking pipeline). This is a real, diff-grounded behavior/contract change (network dependency + different artifact), but it’s not inherently a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] An already-shipped migration was edited to add `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics`, changing its semantics from create-if-absent to drop-and-recreate. Any environment that has not yet run this migration loses existing `top_topics` data when it runs; this edit rode along inside an unrelated embedding PR with no stated intent to alter the migration's behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff edits an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it, which can cause data loss if `top_topics` exists with data when this migration runs (whereas the prior version would not drop/recreate). This is a semantic change to a previously-existing migration file and is unrelated to the embedding changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] An already-shipped migration file was touched in this PR purely for whitespace and removal of the trailing newline, a no-op edit unrelated to the embedding feature. The diff carries silent noise that misrepresents what the PR does: future git blame/bisect on this migration points at the embedding change, and reviewers waste effort hunting for a behavioral change that does not exist.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows an existing migration `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` was modified only by whitespace cleanup (removing trailing spaces) and it now lacks a trailing newline (`\ No newline at end of file`). This is unrelated to the embedding feature and creates review/blame noise without behavioral impact.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] cook_method == raw_html returns the post raw, bypassing the entire sanitize/render pipeline, and TopicEmbed.import sets this for all externally-fetched RSS/article content, which is then emitted with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in embed views. Any attacker-controlled markup in the polled feed or in a page fetched by TopicRetriever (script tags, event handlers, javascript: hrefs) is stored and rendered unsanitized on /embed/best — a persistent XSS executing in the embeddable_host origin, the origin that third-party sites iframe by design. skip_validations: true on both create and revise removes the last guard.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `raw_html` cook method that returns `raw` directly in `Post#cook` (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` when creating posts from externally sourced content (RSS/remote fetch) and passes HTML content (`absolutize_urls(url, contents)`) largely unfiltered (RSS path only does `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`). The embed view then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so attacker-controlled markup can be persisted and executed when `/embed/best` is viewed. This is a verifiable persistent XSS risk introduced by the changes; `skip_validations: true` further removes safeguards during create/revise, though the core issue is the intentional raw HTML bypass plus `raw` rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] import interpolates the raw embed URL into an HTML attribute without escaping: `"#{url}"`, and the only gate is the regex `/^https?\:\/\//` which permits quotes, spaces, and angle brackets in the URL. A feed item link like `http://x/'onmouseover='alert(document.cookie)//` passes the scheme regex, is stored via the raw_html cook path without sanitization, and produces an injected attribute/element in the rendered post — stored XSS on the embed page triggered by any feed-supplied link.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends HTML containing an unescaped `url` inside an `href` attribute: `"#{url}"` and only checks `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes/angle brackets/spaces. The created post is stored with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for that method (skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline). The embed view renders `raw post.cooked` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`), so a malicious feed link containing `'` can break out of the attribute and inject HTML/JS, making this a stored XSS reachable via feed import.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] import_remote calls `open(url).read` with no redirect, IP, or scheme constraint; the host allowlist is checked earlier in TopicRetriever against the original URL only, but open() silently follows redirects and re-resolves DNS. A page on embeddable_host (or any attacker page whose referer matches embeddable_host) can trigger a server-side fetch that 302-redirects (or DNS-rebinds after the host check) to 169.254.169.254, localhost, or internal services; the response body is parsed by Readability and portions (title/content) end up rendered in the embed page, leaking internal network data via SSRF. Note the /^https?\/\// gate in import runs only after the fetch has already happened.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb) with no redirect / IP range / scheme enforcement. The only host check shown is in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, which compares `URI(@embed_url).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` before calling `import_remote` (lib/topic_retriever.rb). That check does not prevent `open(url)` from following HTTP redirects (or re-resolving DNS) to internal/localhost/metadata IPs after the initial allowed-host check. The fetched body is then imported and rendered via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in the embed view (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), so this can leak SSRF response content. Additionally, the `import` method’s `/^https?\:\/\//` URL gate happens after the fetch in `import_remote`, so it doesn’t mitigate the SSRF.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` fetches an admin-set config URL with no scheme validation and no SSRF guard, and its content is fed to SimpleRSS and then into raw_html posts. SiteSetting.feed_polling_url is config-backed attacker-controllable input in the threat model: a compromised admin session (or XSS in the admin UI) can point it at an internal endpoint to exfiltrate response data through imported topics, or at a feed whose items carry XSS payloads that the raw_html path renders verbatim (see the cook_method bypass).
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` fetches a configurable URL without validation/SSRF protections, allowing an attacker who can control that setting to make the server request arbitrary internal/external URLs. This is the same underlying SSRF issue described in the golden comment (extra XSS discussion is additional but doesn’t change the core match).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] postMessage origin validation uses `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, a substring containment test instead of an equality test against a parsed origin. The check accepts any e.origin that appears anywhere inside the discourseUrl string rather than matching the exact origin, so any embedding page whose origin is a substring of the configured URL (e.g. a subdomain sibling sharing the suffix) can post fabricated resize messages. Impact is limited to iframe height spoofing, but the containment comparison is the wrong control shape.
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying flaw: origin validation relies on a substring/indexOf check rather than exact origin matching, which can be bypassed by crafting a malicious domain that passes the containment test (e.g., lookalike/suffix-matching domains).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The embed authorization control compares `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` without normalizing case or trailing port, while the same host string is checked again in TopicRetriever#invalid_host? — two independently hand-maintained copies of the host allowlist. An admin who stores embeddable_host with different case or an explicit port from what browsers send in Referer gets a silent total lockout of embedding (availability failure of the control rather than a bypass), and any future tightening of one check (e.g. scheme validation) silently diverges from the other, which is exactly the drift that later produces a bypass.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, embedding is authorized only if `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (string equality). In `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, retrieval is likewise gated by `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`. Both checks are duplicated and both compare the parsed host (no port) to the raw stored setting without normalization. If an admin configures `embeddable_host` with an explicit port (e.g. `example.com:443`) or with differing case, the equality check will fail and embedding/retrieval will be blocked (availability failure). This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff in `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb` and `lib/topic_retriever.rb`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The two 'valid host' tests stub the private methods under test (retrieved_recently? and perform_retrieve), so the assertions are tautologies that verify nothing about the real code. 'calls perform_retrieve if it hasn't been retrieved recently' stubs retrieved_recently? to return false and then asserts perform_retrieve is called — the test passes even if the real retrieve logic is inverted or broken, because the real gate and the real redis setnx/expire throttle logic are never executed. The actual throttle semantics (60s window, no_throttle override for staff, redis key leak on setnx without expire) have zero coverage in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the "calls perform_retrieve if it hasn't been retrieved recently" and "doesn't call perform_retrieve if it's been retrieved recently" examples stub TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? and then assert expectations about perform_retrieve, making them largely tautological and not exercising the real throttle/Redis logic in lib/topic_retriever.rb (setnx/expire/no_throttle path). However, the finding's claim about "setnx without expire" is not supported by the diff because retrieved_recently? does call $redis.expire when setnx succeeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every test in poll_feed_spec stubs poll_feed out, so the entire body of the new poll_feed method (RSS parsing, url fallback to i.id, content scrubbing, TopicEmbed.import invocation) is never executed by any test. The 'delegates to poll_feed' test only proves execute calls a method — the real RSS-handling logic added in this diff (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:27-39), including the i.link/i.id fallback and CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) which crashes on feeds whose items lack a content element, ships with no test that would catch a regression.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, all examples exercise only Jobs::PollFeed#execute and either expect poll_feed to be never called (first three tests) or merely that it is called once ("delegates to poll_feed"). No test invokes or asserts behavior of the actual poll_feed implementation added in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb (SimpleRSS.parse/open, item link/id fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), TopicEmbed.import calls). So the core RSS-handling logic ships untested, which is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern (though not itself a proven defect).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'creates a topic view when a topic_id is found' test verifies only that the TopicView.new mock was constructed with specific args, asserting the mock interaction rather than any rendered behavior. The real TopicView is never built and the embed/best.html.erb template (new in this diff) is never rendered with real data — the view's posts.present? branching, avatar/username rendering, and the case where a topic exists with zero posts (the 'start_discussion' branch) are all untested and would break silently.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb, the "creates a topic view when a topic_id is found" example uses `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})`, which only asserts the constructor call rather than exercising real `TopicView` behavior or rendering. The newly added template app/views/embed/best.html.erb contains nontrivial branching (`if @topic_view.posts.present?` / else) and renders fields like `post.user.small_avatar_url`, `post.user.username`, and `raw post.cooked`, but no test in the diff renders the view with real `@topic_view` data to cover those branches (including the zero-posts case). This is a concrete test coverage gap introduced alongside new embed view behavior, not a directly verifiable runtime bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The error-path assertions use bare response.should_not be_success, which passes for any non-2xx outcome and does not verify the specific 404/InvalidAccess contract the tests claim to check. The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test would still pass if params.require(:embed_url) produced an unhandled 500 instead of the intended 404 — the tests cannot distinguish the promised error semantics from a crash, giving false confidence in the ensure_embeddable error path.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the error-path examples (e.g., `it "is 404 without an embed_url"` and others) assert only `response.should_not be_success`, which will pass for any non-2xx response and does not verify the stated contract ("is 404"). Given `EmbedController#best` calls `params.require(:embed_url)`, a change that turned the behavior into a 400/500 could still satisfy `should_not be_success`, so the tests provide weak/ambiguous coverage of the intended error semantics. This is a test robustness issue, not an application defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update test asserts the revised content but never asserts that content_sha1 was persisted or that importing identical content skips the revision, leaving the new sha1-comparison branch half-verified. A regression in the content_sha1 update (topic_embed.rb:44 embed.update_column) or in the unchanged-content short-circuit (content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1) would pass this suite — e.g. if update_column were removed, every poll would silently rewrite the post and the tests would still be green; the 'import is idempotent' property the sha1 exists to provide is never asserted.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import` the sha1-based idempotency logic is new and nontrivial: it only revises the post when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` and then persists the new sha via `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` (topic_embed.rb around the update branch). The added spec `Supports updating the post` only asserts the post content changed (`post.cooked` matches /new contents/) and never asserts (a) `topic_embeds.content_sha1` was updated after a revision, nor (b) that re-importing identical `contents` does not call `PostRevisor` / does not rewrite the post. So a regression removing `update_column` or breaking the unchanged-content short-circuit could still leave tests green. This is a concrete missing-test gap rather than a demonstrated runtime defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1 sets every existing post to cook_method=1, which per Post.cook_methods Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html) is :raw_html. After this migration runs, every pre-existing post in the database is silently reclassified as raw HTML: Post#cook (app/models/post.rb:131-134) returns raw uncooked text for cook_method == :raw_html, so all historical markdown posts render their raw markdown source to users. The default should be 0 (:regular); the migration backfills the entire table with the wrong value and there is no correcting backfill step.

adjudication.rationale: The finding hinges on the claim that `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` maps `:regular` to 0 and `:raw_html` to 1, making the migration default (`default: 1`) equal to `:raw_html`. The diff does not support that mapping. In fact, existing code uses the same `Enum` pattern for `Post.types` (`Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)`), and in Discourse this convention is typically 1-based (e.g., regular posts commonly have `post_type = 1`). Under that (implied) convention, `default: 1` corresponds to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`, so the described mass reclassification/markdown breakage is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] An already-shipped migration is modified in this diff to add force: true to create_table :top_topics. Any environment that re-runs this migration (e.g. migrating a database where the version row was rolled back, or a deploy replay) executes DROP TABLE top_topics and recreates it, destroying all computed top-topic ranking data with no backup or export step. A shipped migration must never be made destructive; the force: true flag belongs only in the new migration for fresh environments, not by editing the historical one.

adjudication.rationale: The diff edits an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it. Because this is a historical migration file (not a new migration), re-running it in any scenario where the migration is executed again against a DB that already has `top_topics` would destroy existing `top_topics` data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] create_table :topic_embeds uses force: true, making the migration destructive on re-run, and the table defines topic_id/post_id as plain integers with no foreign keys or dependent cleanup. Re-running the migration drops any populated topic_embeds rows (losing the embed_url→topic mapping, which then causes TopicRetriever/EmbedController to re-import duplicate topics). Additionally, when a topic or post is deleted there is no cascade or cleanup hook, leaving orphaned topic_embeds rows whose topic_id_for_embed lookups return dead topic ids for EmbedController#best.

adjudication.rationale: The new `topic_embeds` table is created with `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which will drop/recreate the table if the migration is re-run (destructive). Also, `TopicEmbed` only has `belongs_to :topic`/`:post` with no DB foreign keys and no Rails-level dependent cleanup; `topic_id_for_embed` blindly returns a `topic_id` that `EmbedController#best` passes into `TopicView.new(...)`. If the referenced topic/post is deleted, an orphaned `topic_embeds` row can cause lookups to return a dead topic id, leading to broken embed behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The throttle key is committed via $redis.setnx before perform_retrieve runs, so a failed or failed-early retrieval still marks the embed_url as 'retrieved' and blocks all retries for 60 seconds If import_remote raises or the user lookup returns nil on the first attempt, subsequent embed page loads within 60s skip retrieval entirely; the throttle key expires but each retry re-arms it, so a persistently failing URL is retried at most once per 60s per visitor with no error recorded anywhere

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, `retrieved_recently?` is evaluated before `perform_retrieve` (`perform_retrieve unless (invalid_host? || retrieved_recently?)`). `retrieved_recently?` sets the Redis key via `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and expires it for 60s on the first call. If `perform_retrieve` then returns early (e.g., `fetch_http` finds `user.blank?` and `return`) or raises (e.g., `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`open(url)`), the throttle key remains set, causing subsequent calls within 60s to skip retrieval even though nothing was successfully retrieved.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The update path advances embed.content_sha1 to the new digest even when revisor.revise! returns false without revising (should_revise? false, e.g. post deleted), permanently discarding the new content Once the sha1 is updated while the post write was skipped, every future poll sees an unchanged digest and the remote article's edits are silently dropped forever while the feed poll reports success

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update branch does `revisor.revise!(...)` and then unconditionally executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` when the digest differs. The diff also shows `PostRevisor#revise!` returns `false` early if `should_revise?` is false (and performs no update). Therefore, if `revise!` is skipped/fails, the code can still advance `content_sha1`, causing subsequent polls to treat the content as unchanged and never retry updating the post—effectively dropping remote edits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed has no error handling around the parse or per-item import loop and the job is declared sidekiq_options retry: false, so any single malformed item (nil content -> NoMethodError on i.content.scrub, or a non-HTTP i.id GUID like 'tag:...') aborts the remaining items with no retry and no user-visible error One bad feed entry silently drops the rest of that poll cycle every hour; items after the failing one are never imported and nothing surfaces the failure to the operator

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates `rss.items.each`, calling `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. There is no rescue around the network fetch/parse or the per-item loop, so any exception (e.g., `open`/parse errors, or `i.content` being nil causing `NoMethodError` on `.scrub`) will abort the entire job and skip remaining items for that run. This is compounded by `sidekiq_options retry: false`, meaning failures won’t be retried by Sidekiq and nothing in this diff surfaces/logs an operator-visible error. (The specific claim about non-HTTP `i.id` aborting is not strictly supported because `TopicEmbed.import` returns early on non-HTTP URLs, but other exception paths are clearly present.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] import_remote calls open(url).read with no timeout and no size cap on a user-triggered path (the embed controller enqueues RetrieveTopic for every visitor URL) A slow or hanging remote host blocks the Sidekiq worker indefinitely (open-uri default has no read timeout for this usage), and a huge response is fully read into memory before parsing, exhausting the worker

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which does `open(url).read` (in `app/models/topic_embed.rb`) without any timeout or response-size limiting, then passes the full body into `Readability::Document`. This method is reachable from a user-triggered flow: `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` when no embed exists, which calls `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, which calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`. A slow/hanging remote server can therefore tie up a Sidekiq worker, and a very large response will be fully read into memory before parsing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) has no timeout or download-size cap on the hourly scheduled job A hung or enormous feed permanently wedges the PollFeed scheduled worker slot each cycle instead of failing fast

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added scheduled job `Jobs::PollFeed` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), the feed is fetched via `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` using `open-uri` with no explicit timeouts, size limits, or other fail-fast controls. Since this job runs `hourly` and performs network I/O synchronously, a slow/hung connection or extremely large response can block the Sidekiq worker thread for an extended time and repeatedly impact scheduled execution. This reliability/availability defect is introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The loading page reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely and the retrieval job's failure (invalid host, nil user, fetch error, throttled skip) never renders any error or terminal state When retrieval fails permanently the embedding site shows an endless 'Loading Discussion...' loop with no indication anything is wrong, and every reload re-enqueues a RetrieveTopic job forever

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `TopicEmbed` exists it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The loading template unconditionally reloads the page every 30 seconds (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), so if the embed can never be created (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early because `embed_by_username` user is blank, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` raises on `open(url)`, or other permanent retrieval failures), the iframe will stay in an infinite “Loading Discussion...” loop with no terminal/error state and will keep re-enqueuing retrieve jobs on every reload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When PostCreator#create returns nil inside the transaction, the code silently continues (embed never created, post stays nil) and import returns nil with no log or error result PollFeed treats the item as processed and moves on; the embed page keeps serving the loading loop with no record that topic creation failed

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the creation path wraps `PostCreator.new(...).create` in a transaction and only creates the `TopicEmbed` row if `post.present?` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). If `create` returns `nil`/blank, the method returns `nil` with no logging or error propagation. Callers like `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` ignore the return value and continue iterating (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), so failures are silent and the embed UI can stay in the "loading" state if no `TopicEmbed` is ever created (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb + loading.html.erb). However, the finding’s claim that PollFeed “treats the item as processed” is overstated—there’s no persisted per-item processed state in the diff, so it would simply try again on the next run/request. The real issue is missing failure reporting/handling for post creation failures, not a provable one-time loss of processing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The update path calls embed.post and passes it to PostRevisor without a nil check, so a deleted post raises NoMethodError inside the poll/retrieve job A remote article whose topic was deleted makes every PollFeed cycle and every RetrieveTopic job for that URL raise, repeatedly failing the job with a raw exception instead of a handled skip

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing `TopicEmbed` record is found, the code does `post = embed.post` and then (if content changed) calls `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!` without checking whether `embed.post` is nil. If the associated `Post` has been deleted (no FK enforcement shown; `post_id` is just an integer), `embed.post` will be nil and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` / subsequent calls will raise (e.g., NoMethodError). This affects callers like `Jobs::PollFeed` and `TopicRetriever` which repeatedly invoke import logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key is dead code: it is defined but never called anywhere in the diff, and the Modified-since behavior it implies (skipping unchanged feeds) was never implemented The next maintainer assumes feed polling is incremental because the key exists and builds on it; deleting the method removes the misleading implication at zero cost

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `def feed_key` is defined (building a `feed-modified:` Redis key from `feed_polling_url`) but is never referenced by `execute` or `poll_feed`, and no other diff hunk calls it. This makes it dead code and its naming suggests incremental/modified-since behavior that the shown implementation does not perform (it always `open`s and parses the feed). Removing it would reduce misleading maintenance surface without changing behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The fallback 'url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?/' assigns the entry id, which for Atom feeds is commonly a non-URL URN (tag:...), and TopicEmbed.import then silently returns nil for it with no log Atom feeds whose ids are URNs are silently skipped every hour with no error result and no log line identifying which item was dropped

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed, the code falls back to `url = i.id` when `i.link` is blank or not an http(s) URL (`url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`). TopicEmbed.import immediately returns nil unless the URL matches `^https?\:\/\//`. For Atom feeds, `id` is often a URN (e.g., `tag:...`), so this fallback will cause the item to be dropped (TopicEmbed.import returns nil) with no logging/handling in poll_feed. This is a real, diff-grounded correctness bug that can silently skip feed entries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every visitor to a not-yet-imported embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job (throttled only by the 60s redis key for non-staff), and the throttle key persists even when retrieval fails, coupling page-render behavior to job success with no observability on the enqueue path A popularly-linked but unimportable URL generates a continuous stream of jobs and reloads that all end in the loading loop, with no counter or log distinguishing 'not yet imported' from 'permanently failing'

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` on every request when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, then renders `loading` which auto-reloads after 30s (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`). Throttling only occurs inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` in the job (via a 60s Redis key), so the enqueue path itself is unthrottled and can still create many queued jobs for a popular URL. Also, `retrieved_recently?` sets the Redis key before `perform_retrieve`; if `fetch_http`/`open(url)` fails, there’s no failure state recorded and the page will keep showing the loading loop with repeated enqueues, with no explicit logging/observability in the controller/job code shown.
